_meta.command: node harness.js testbed 500 release ref --json=dev/runs/release-panel.json --v54 --snab --slope (run in 4 pieces with --part=I/4; python3 dev/tools/merge_parts.py)

v422.label: TODAY (v4.22, Hub spec): the s34 main row (wage contribution)

release.label: RELEASE (v5.4): Compassionism with every mechanism, paid for by the Source; households and children; job loss and re-employment, PTH's books, PTF by sector

v53.label: v5.3's main row: no job loss and re-employment, PTH and PTF as in v5.3 (the risk measures still reported)

cut0.label: no pay cut on return to work (people find work at their old pay)

cut20.label: a 20% pay cut on return to work (the design value is 10%)

autopay.label: automation as a lasting pay drag instead of job loss (the earlier rule)

pthbold.label: Acre Equity growing by the earlier 3-5% rule instead of the price rise + 2%

ptfs25.label: PTF cutting prices 25% in transport, health care and childcare (no Hub figure; the main row assumes no cut there)

dis.label: a disaster in Year 7: a quarter of households lose $10,000 of property and four weeks of work (FEMA data; a scenario, not a model part)

h1.label: H1: every dollar the Source pays backed by new output

face.label: essentials bought with BU counted as backed by output

tax.label: paid for by a flat contribution on wages instead of the Source

cost.label: creative projects counted at the cost of their hours, not at market value (the cautious reading)

cap5.label: community-business capacity growing only as reinvestment pays for it (the 5-year rule)

all.label: taking part costs nothing (every adult joins)

free.label: price cuts free (PTF and PTH cuts counted as capacity, not a transfer)

standins.label: the two former stand-ins on (octave wage raise and inflation damping; theoretical, off by default)

sav.label: savings that keep up with prices (interest = inflation + 0.97% a year, in both runs)

sav0.label: savings that only keep their value (interest = inflation, in both runs)

idx.label: the BU indexed to prices every year (the Hub indexes it only in a year prices rise faster than 5%)

h1idx.label: H1 with the BU indexed every year

mid.label: middle backing reading: new output backs the Source's payout up to 12% of earned income a year (the Kenya study's two-year rollout)

midlo.label: middle band, low end: up to 8% a year (all of the US's underused labour, BLS U-6, 2025)

midhi.label: middle band, high end: up to 16% a year (the Kenya study's peak year)

slack.label: the spending layer in normal years too: idle labour (U-6 above its lowest level, 1.1% of wages) filled at the normal-times multiplier 0.6

hcap.label: landlords raise the rent of tenants paying with BU by $0.50 per BU dollar spent on rent, outside PTH (housing-voucher evidence: Collinson and Ganong 2018)

hcaphi.label: rents outside PTH rise $1.41 per BU dollar spent on rent, for every renter outside PTH (Susin 2002: other renters paid more than the subsidy)

rev10.label: 10% of high conversion rates unearned, audits catch half

rev20n.label: 20% of high conversion rates unearned, no audits

giftrun.label: the launch gift paid for over the run (the Source spreads the new money for the gift over the run)

progtax.label: paid for by a progressive income tax instead of the Source (the 2025 federal brackets, scaled up; not specified by the Hub)

landtax.label: paid for by a land-value tax instead of the Source (falling on adults in proportion to their savings; not specified by the Hub)

age.label: households with ageing: children grow up, are born and leave home; estates pass to partners and children (a population that drifts: couples are fixed)

agenone.label: ageing, retirees leave the programme and live on Social Security alone

agepia.label: ageing, with a Social Security benefit linked to the adult's own wage

ageleave.label: ageing, every estate leaving the model (no heirs)

agecps.label: ageing, with wages following US earnings by age (BLS CPS)

fixr.label: automation risk linked to wages (lower-paid jobs at higher risk, as in the occupation data)

fixs.label: wages spread as widely as in the US wealth survey

fixm.label: wages centred on the US survey's median ($54,698 instead of $39,945)

fixall.label: the three wage and risk readings together

v52.label: v5.2's main row: adults living alone, BU buying food, housing and medical care, their own starting savings, everyone paying the full basket

adults.label: adults living alone (no households), otherwise the main row

core.label: BU buying only food, housing and medical care (v5.2's list)

indiv.label: each adult keeping their own money (no pooling)

cb50.label: a child allowance of half the adult BU

wmodel.label: households' starting savings from the model's own draw (not the SCF)

nosg.label: everyone paying their full cost each year whatever their income (no income-graded spending)

shock50.label: partners' income swings moving together strongly (0.5)

fbs50.label: FBS50 spread evenly over its range (more adults need a larger surplus to advance)

sv.label: no programme, savings that keep up with prices

sv0.label: no programme, savings that keep only their value

ag.label: no programme, households with ageing (children's lives; estates to heirs)

agpia.label: no programme, households with ageing, a benefit linked to the adult's own wage

agleave.label: no programme, households with ageing, every estate leaving the model

agcps.label: no programme, households with ageing and earnings by age

ltr.label: no programme, automation risk linked to wages

lts.label: no programme, the SCF's wider spread of wages

ltm.label: no programme, wages centred on the US survey's median

lta.label: no programme, the three wage and risk readings

b52.label: no programme, v5.2's population: adults living alone, their own starting savings, everyone paying the full basket

badults.label: no programme, adults living alone (with income-graded spending)

bindiv.label: no programme, each adult keeping their own money

bwmodel.label: no programme, households' starting savings from the model's own draw

bnosg.label: no programme, everyone paying their full cost

bshock50.label: no programme, partners' income swings moving together strongly (0.5)

b53.label: no programme, v5.3's: no job loss and re-employment (the risk measures still reported)

bcut0.label: no programme, no pay cut on return to work

bcut20.label: no programme, a 20% pay cut on return to work

bautopay.label: no programme, automation as a lasting pay drag instead of job loss

bdis.label: no programme, a disaster in Year 7
